951985500.contact: not stated on the page read

951985500.geographic_limits: Not stated on the page read; all examples are US communities, and about 40 percent of grants go to rural places.

951985500.name: AARP

priorities: Livable communities for people of all ages, especially 50 and older
Public spaces such as parks and community gardens

953255038.accepts_evidence: Toyota's grant guidelines say Toyota USA Foundation grants are by invitation only, and applicants need an invitation and a code to enter the online system (https://www.toyota.com/usa/sustainability/community/grant-guidelines-applications/overview).
953255038.conflicts_with_return: The return is not marked preselected-only and names a contact with no deadline; the site says foundation grants are by invitation only. Exclusions broadly match.
953255038.contact: None for grants; Toyota says it cannot answer individual phone, mail or email inquiries. Portal support only.
953255038.deadlines: None for the foundation. Toyota budgets by a year ending March 31 and says decisions can take up to six months.
953255038.eligibility: Under Toyota's general rules: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, state or municipal bodies and public schools; one grant per twelve months. The foundation is said to have its own, tighter guidelines, which are not spelled out.
953255038.geographic_limits: United States only. The pages read do not name the foundation's target communities.
953255038.how_to_apply: Foundation: wait for an invitation and code. Separate from the foundation, Toyota's manufacturing plants run community grant programs that take online applications without an invitation from organizations in the plant's own state.
953255038.name: Toyota USA Foundation
953255038.not_funded: Under Toyota's general rules: individuals; groups serving only their own members (fraternal, labor, religious); athletic or sports teams; political parties or candidates; publications, lobbying, advertising; capital campaigns; endowments; individual fundraising efforts; vehicle donation requests.
953255038.notes: Closed to cold applications. The site describes the foundation as a $100 million endowment begun in 1987. The same guidelines page also covers Toyota Motor North America and Toyota Financial Services (both invitation only) and ten plant communities with open local programs, among them the Texas plant (TMMTX). A Texas youth or workforce program has a better chance through the plant's community grants or a local Toyota relationship than through the foundation.
priorities: STEM education from preschool through post-secondary
Driving Possibilities, a long-term career readiness initiative
Emphasis on women and diverse communities
953255038.types_of_support: Monetary grants, with employee volunteering and Toyota know-how alongside

953792725.accepts_evidence: The FAQ says applications are taken at any time during the year through the online form on the grants page, with a first-phase review inside eight weeks (https://dev.la84.org/faq/). Read from a development copy of the site; the live grants page could not be opened.
953792725.confidence: low - grant rules come from an undated development copy of the site; the live grants page was refused by the fetch tool
953792725.contact: No grants contact on the pages read (the return lists grants@la84.org).
953792725.deadlines: No fixed deadline per the FAQ; the full process usually takes 3 to 6 months.
953792725.eligibility: 501(c)(3) public charities (not private foundations), or groups using a fiscal agent; good standing with California authorities; a written policy on preventing child sexual abuse in youth sports; extra rules for soccer, hockey, lacrosse, boxing, rugby, football and martial arts. A declined applicant or a grantee may reapply after 12 months.
953792725.geographic_limits: Programs must take place in Southern California's eight counties: Imperial, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara and Ventura. The applicant's headquarters may be elsewhere.
953792725.grant_range_stated: Most grants are $10,000 or less; larger for more complex programs. About 90 grants a year.
953792725.how_to_apply: Read the grant guidelines and FAQ, then submit the online application; a second phase asks for budgets, financial statements and a board list, and a site visit is required for proposals under active review.
953792725.name: LA84 Foundation
953792725.not_funded: Individuals; single schools or single-school sites; for-profits; travel outside Southern California; land purchase; debt; endowments; political or legislative activity; sectarian or fraternal purposes; federated appeals. General operating support very rarely. Camps, one-time clinics and elite or club programs are not priorities.
953792725.notes: Check www.la84.org/grants by hand before relying on this. The live pages that opened carried only menus (Grants, Play Equity Fund). The rules above may be older than the current site, and the live site may now run timed grant cycles instead of year-round intake. Funding is limited to youth sports in Southern California, so a national organization needs a Southern California program to qualify.
953792725.page_dated: The pages read are undated and sit on dev.la84.org; the live site has been redesigned and now also lists a Play Equity Fund
priorities: Sport exploration and exposure for youth
953792725.types_of_support: Program costs, sports equipment, renovation of sports facilities and fields

956089998.accepts_evidence: Organizations that fit the funding guidelines are told to submit a Letter of Inquiry through the online portal; every LOI gets a preliminary screening and those that may qualify are invited within 30 days to send a full proposal (https://theahmansonfoundation.org/letter-of-inquiry/ and https://theahmansonfoundation.org/preliminary-screening/)
956089998.contact: The Ahmanson Foundation, 9215 Wilshire Boulevard, Beverly Hills, CA 90210; 310-278-0770; info@theahmansonfoundation.org
956089998.deadlines: not stated (no deadlines listed; LOI screening answers within 30 days)
956089998.eligibility: 501(c)(3) public charities (not private foundations) classified under 509(a)(1) or 509(a)(2); operating at least 3-5 years; established, stable leadership. Must wait 12-18 months from the decision date of any earlier request, approved or declined.
956089998.geographic_limits: Los Angeles County: applicants must be based in and serving Los Angeles County
956089998.how_to_apply: Review the funding guidelines and eligibility pages, then submit an LOI in the online portal: dated letter, contacts, a 1-3 page narrative on the organization and the request, and a project budget. If invited, submit a full proposal.
956089998.name: The Ahmanson Foundation
956089998.not_funded: Individuals; religious organizations for sectarian purposes or serving a single denomination; lobbying, political activity, voter registration, advocacy organizations. Generally not approved: endowed chairs, fellowships, internships, individual scholarships; annual campaigns or ongoing operating support; film, video and media production; deficits, loans, debt reduction; re-granting; traveling exhibitions, performance underwriting, seminars, workshops, surveys, general research; regional or national charities; disease-specific or medical research; pilot projects; general solicitations; fundraising or awards events
956089998.notes: Strictly Los Angeles County, and regional or national charities are generally not approved. A national organization would need an LA County-based affiliate with its own public charity status and a capital-type request.
priorities: Preference for one-time or short-term requests, mainly capital needs
956089998.types_of_support: Mainly capital: construction and renovation, equipment and furnishings, program vehicles, technology, program supplies. Program or operating support only occasionally, for organizations with established outstanding programs. Capital campaigns considered once 60-80% funded and completable within a year.
